text:
sre-oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High tail latency detected on /v1/generate-stream — p95 and p99 breaching SLO. Paging #eng-runtime #eng-sre. Customers might see streaming stalls. :rotating_light:

maria: ack, I'm on call. pulling dashboards now. can someone post affected routes?

aj: looking — short summary: p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~650ms in last 4m, p99 ~2.1s -> ~7.8s. error rate up slightly, streaming sessions show stall spikes and WS disconnects. metric ids: route=generate-stream, model=redwood-open-13b, region=us-west1.

cheng: thanks. is this concentrated on streaming or also non-stream token gen?

aj: primarily streaming. non-stream text gen p99 up but not as bad (1.2s -> 2.6s). streaming tail has lots of long GC/CPU spikes in preproc.

maria: putting together impact table. preliminary list: mobile-chat (prod), legal-assistant (prod), analytics-explorer (staging but hitting dedicated). will DM account team.

dan: any logs from preproc/tokenizer svc? last time similar was tokenizer queue overflow.

leo: pasting recent logs (truncated):
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] tokenize_worker: queue_len=1248 processing_latency_ms=842 cpu_ms=780 model_input_size=58
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] preproc: template_render_ms=2300 json_mode_parser_ms=1900 tool_schema_resolve_ms=1100
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] ws: write_timeout, conn_id=abcd1234, client=10.2.3.45
```

maria: wow template_render and json parser are huge. maybe a bad incoming payload? any recent deploys to prompt-builder or template-service?

aj: no deploys in last 2 hours. but we got a spike in requests with large tool schemas and deeply nested JSON-mode templates. could be a customer regression.

cheng: triage plan: 1) short-term mitigation to reduce customer impact, 2) find offending payloads, 3) roll back or patch. who can try live mitigations?

dan: I can run mitigation steps. proposing: throttle streaming concurrency for the model tier, enable fallback to non-streaming endpoint for suspicious clients, and temporarily disable JSON mode parsing in preproc for incoming streaming requests.

leo: we can also temporarily scale preproc workers and enable prefix KV caching for frequent prompts. scaling command: `kubectl scale deployment/preproc --replicas=6 -n inference`

maria: do that and leave me in loop. also please add a rate-limit rule for /v1/generate-stream higher cost buckets. `rb infra rate-limit create --route /v1/generate-stream --limit 10rps --scope customer_heavy`

aj: started a focused query to find biggest payloads:
```sql
SELECT client_id, count(*) as cnt, avg(len(payload)) as avg_len
FROM request_logs
WHERE route = '/v1/generate-stream' AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY client_id
ORDER BY cnt desc
LIMIT 10;
```

leo: scaling preproc now. also rolling restart of template-render service: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/template-render -n inference`

sre-oncall-bot: ONCALL HANDOFF REMINDER: @cheng will be primary incident lead in 30m unless overridden.

maria: handoff fine with me. aj keep digging on payloads. dan coordinate with infra to enforce rate limits.

dan: applied a quick customer-scoped rate-limit for the top offender (client=x-legal-prod) to 8rps. reaction :thumbsup:. also enabled fallback routing to redwood-open-13b-fast variant for streaming requests that exceed size threshold.

aj: found 2 clients with median payload size 6x normal. sample payload id=pl_9a8b with huge tool_schema (350kb) + complex JSON-mode template. saving payload to /var/tmp/incident_2965432101/pl_9a8b.json for analysis.

leo: note: complex tool schemas blow up template render time due to full schema validation in JSON mode. suggestion: short-term patch to bypass deep schema validation for streaming endpoints (fast-path).

cheng: good. can we patch a config toggle instead of full change? toggle `TEMPLATE_VALIDATE_DEPTH=2` and restart workers. less blast radius.

dan: toggled `TEMPLATE_VALIDATE_DEPTH=2` on preproc staging canaries, CPU dropped ~35% on canary pods. rolling out to 50% of preproc pool.

maria: customer comms: ops-alert sent to affected customers, we flagged degraded streaming for certain workflows and provided temporary mitigation steps. account leads pinged.

aj: after scaling + toggle + rate-limits, p95 dropped to ~220ms, p99 ~1.4s in 10m window. streaming disconnects down. still higher than baseline but improving.

leo: logging note: we should add size-based fast-fail earlier in preproc to avoid heavy template/JSON-mode work for streaming. draft PR idea: `if payload_size > 200k then route_non_stream` with metrics.

cheng: agree. owners: aj for analytics query and payload hunting, leo for infra scaling and fast-fail PR, dan for rate-limit & config toggles, maria for customer comms and impact thread. I'll coordinate postmortem.

maria: handover to @cheng in 20m — please update `#incidents` summary when you handoff.

dan: one more quick mitigation we applied: enabled KV prefix caching on the most common prompt templates (`CACHE_PREFIX=true`) — seems to cut repeated render time by ~60% on canary.

aj: saving traces and flamegraphs to s3://redwood-incident-logs/2965432101/ for postmortem.

maria: thanks all. continuing to monitor. if p99 goes above 3s again, escalate to SEV2. reaction :eyes:

sre-oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations in progress. incident severity set to SEV3 -> monitoring. oncall rota noted.

cheng: taking ownership now. I'll collate timeline and assign postmortem. good work on quick mitigations.

leo: PRs to follow: fast-fail payload size check, shallow schema validation toggle, and metric for template_render_ms by client_id.

maria: closing loop with customers after we confirm stable metrics for 30m.

(incident thread continues in handoff doc)
